readingInstruction: Read Psalm 24. This psalm moves from the creation to the clean-handed worshiper to the King of glory entering the gates. Read the second half as a call and response, with different voices asking and answering.
settingTheScene: Psalm 24 is a psalm of David, likely sung when the ark of the covenant was brought up to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6). It is a processional psalm with three parts: the LORD’s ownership of the earth (vv. 1-2), the character of those who may approach him (vv. 3-6), and the entry of the King (vv. 7-10). It pairs naturally with Psalm 15 and with James’s call to purity of heart. Christians have long read it as a picture of Christ’s ascension.
observation: “The earth is the LORD’s and the fullness thereof, the world and those who dwell therein” (v. 1).
“Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And who shall stand in his holy place?” (v. 3).
“He who has clean hands and a pure heart” (v. 4).
“He will receive blessing from the LORD and righteousness from the God of his salvation” (v. 5).
“Lift up your heads, O gates! And be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of glory may come in” (v. 7).
“Who is this King of glory? The LORD, strong and mighty, the LORD, mighty in battle!” (v. 8).
“Who is this King of glory? The LORD of hosts, he is the King of glory!” (v. 10).
“For he has founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers” (v. 2).
interpretation:
The psalm starts with the biggest claim possible: “The earth is the LORD’s and the fullness thereof, the world and those who dwell therein, for he has founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers.” Everything belongs to God, including us. Nothing in the world is outside his claim. So the question is: how can anyone come to the One who owns all things?

“Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And who shall stand in his holy place? He who has clean hands and a pure heart, who does not lift up his soul to what is false and does not swear deceitfully.” Clean hands refer to actions, and a pure heart refers to motives. This is the same standard as Psalm 15, and James echoes it when he calls for cleansing hands and purifying hearts (James 4:8). Such a person “will receive blessing from the LORD and righteousness from the God of his salvation.” Even this righteousness is a gift from the God of his salvation. Such is “the generation of those who seek him, who seek the face of the God of Jacob.”

Then the procession arrives at the gates. A voice cries: “Lift up your heads, O gates! And be lifted up, O ancient doors, that the King of glory may come in!” A watchman replies: “Who is this King of glory?” And the answer comes: “The LORD, strong and mighty, the LORD, mighty in battle!” The call is repeated, and the answer enlarges: “The LORD of hosts, he is the King of glory!” The psalm leaves us at the threshold with the King entering.

Christians have long seen in this the ascension of Christ. The only one with truly clean hands and a pure heart is Jesus. He ascended the hill, was received into the Father’s presence, and entered the gates in victory after conquering sin and death. And because he has entered as our forerunner, we can follow him. The King of glory is also the one who welcomes the humble to his side. The gates open for him, and through him they open for us.
connection: Psalm 15 is the companion psalm. 1 Corinthians 10:26 quotes verse 1. 2 Samuel 6:12-15 describes the ark entering Jerusalem. Isaiah 6:1-5 shows a holy King and an unclean people. Matthew 5:8 blesses the pure in heart. James 4:8 calls for cleansing of hands and hearts. Ephesians 4:8-10 and Acts 1:9-11 describe the ascension. Hebrews 4:14, 6:19-20, and 9:24 speak of Christ entering heaven as forerunner. 1 Corinthians 15:57 gives thanks for victory. Revelation 5:11-13 shows the worship of the King.
application:
Say verse 1 over your day: the earth is the LORD’s and everything in it, including my money, time, and work.

Ask the Lord to give you clean hands and a pure heart, and confess anything he shows you.

Open the gates of your heart to the King of glory, and welcome him in as Lord over one area where you have held back.
prayerPrompts: Tell God you cannot ascend by your own clean hands.
Thank Jesus who ascended for you.
Open the gates of your life to the King of glory.
